title: Competitive entry mosaic and displacement scenarios for emerging open models
creator: Meera Patel
description: Purpose: build a repeatable, quantitative framework that maps how newly released open models (and forks) can enter Redwood’s product surface and displace existing model variants across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Goal is to produce: 1) a competitive entry mosaic (visual + table) that ranks emergent models by integration effort, cost delta, latency profile, and legal/licensing friction; 2) three displacement scenarios (optimistic, base, defensive) with procurement triggers and operational mitigations; 3) a prioritized signal ingestion plan for continuous monitoring.
background: Tactical gap: PM & procurement teams lack a consistent way to reason about short-term supply shocks (model forks, license changes) and longer-term displacement (new-model quality that undercuts our preferred variants). Existing artifacts are fragmented across Confluence notes and one-off spreadsheets. This initiative synthesizes signal types (community traction, GitHub activity, quantized benchmark deltas, license CLA changes, vendor partnerships) into decision-ready artifacts.
scope: In-scope: public/open model releases, forks with non-trivial weight/quantization changes, major license relicensing events, partner-hosted model launch signals. Out-of-scope: closed-source commercial vendor product roadmaps unless surfaced via market telemetry.
methodology: 1) Taxonomy: define 8 signal buckets (quality delta, compute footprint, quantization friendliness, latency tail risk, licensing friction, community velocity, partner distribution, tooling compatibility). 2) Scoring: normalize signals to create a 0-100 entry risk score per model. 3) Scenario construction: map top 12 models into three business-impact scenarios with probability estimates. 4) Operational runbook: procurement triggers, dedicated capacity experiments, fallback routing policies, customer comms templates.
deliverables:
- Competitive entry mosaic (CSV + Confluence visual)
- Displacement scenarios doc with fiscal impact estimates
- Procurement trigger matrix and playbook
- Continuous ingestion plan (data sources + alert thresholds)
- Deck for GTM & Customer Success to align messaging
acceptance_criteria: 1) Mosaic includes at least 12 candidate models with scored signals. 2) Scenarios include modeled cost/loss estimates for Hosted & Dedicated tiers. 3) Procurement trigger matrix lists clear action for >=3 trigger types (license, performance, partner). 4) Onboarding doc for Data Engineering to onboard 3 signals to the ingestion pipeline.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Data freshness vs. precision: early signals are noisy; we trade sensitivity for fewer false positives by smoothing GitHub and Discord signal spikes.
- Resource trade: building full ingestion quickly delays scenario synthesis — prioritized to ship an MVP mosaic first.
- Customer noise: broad public discourse may exaggerate model readiness; scenarios use calibrated internal evals before recommending rollouts.
